name: Cabo Verde
summary: The Civil Code protects a reserved share (legítima) for compulsory heirs, so a will cannot dispose of it. The fractions were not retrieved. Rules for foreigners, trusts and foundations were not sourced.
reserved_share: A legítima is reserved for compulsory heirs and the testator cannot dispose of it (Civil Code succession rules; Cabo Verde information sheet of the Portuguese-language justice network). The shares and heirs were not retrieved; the Portuguese Code's two-thirds should not be assumed.
foreign_law_note: No source found on the conflict rule for foreigners' succession under the Cabo Verde Civil Code.
trust_note: No trust or private-foundation law was found. Answers are provisional.
open_questions: Reserved fractions and who is protected (arts. 2156 ff. equivalent) not retrieved.
Conflict-of-laws rule for foreigners' estates not found.
Trusts, fiducia and foundations in Cabo Verde not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
